atmosphere-a.a1: the mean is held inside the published Moon, Mars and Earth ranges and the width tuned to them (GEN.482)
atmosphere-a.a2: a straight-line law fitted to three Solar System anchors, Earth IW+3.5, Mars IW to IW+1 and Moon IW to IW-2 (GEN.482)

atmosphere-b.b1: the dry carbon bracket is tuned to the bulk silicate Earth's 100 ppm carbon (GEN.813)

atmosphere-k.k7: N2, O2, OCS, SO2, Ar, Kr and Xe come from one measured comet (67P, Rubin 2019) with a design width; the row is partly verified, not flagged stand-in (GEN.520 keeps them as stand-in values)

surface-ground-types.anorthositic: the assemblage is one of Hu, Ehlmann and Seager 2012 Table 2, a library of the Earth's and the Moon's crusts; GEN.474 (rock_types) replaces the fixed assemblages once wired
surface-ground-types.basaltic: the assemblage is one of Hu, Ehlmann and Seager 2012 Table 2, a library of the Earth's and the Moon's crusts; GEN.474 (rock_types) replaces the fixed assemblages once wired
surface-ground-types.felsic: the assemblage is one of Hu, Ehlmann and Seager 2012 Table 2, a library of the Earth's and the Moon's crusts; GEN.474 (rock_types) replaces the fixed assemblages once wired
surface-ground-types.oxidised: the assemblage is one of Hu, Ehlmann and Seager 2012 Table 2, a library of the Earth's and the Moon's crusts; GEN.474 (rock_types) replaces the fixed assemblages once wired
surface-ground-types.ultramafic: the assemblage is one of Hu, Ehlmann and Seager 2012 Table 2, a library of the Earth's and the Moon's crusts; GEN.474 (rock_types) replaces the fixed assemblages once wired

atmosphere-e.e5: solar means the solar-abundance scale the sub-Neptune retrievals are quoted on, no Solar System body is a source

atmosphere-h.h1: solar metals is the abundance scale of the computed equilibrium line
atmosphere-h.h2: solar metals is the abundance scale of the computed equilibrium line

atmosphere-j.j2: the Mars composition is a test value the output is compared with, the weight is the retention physics (Boss, fork 7)
atmosphere-j.j3: the Titan methane share is a test value the output is compared with, the weight is the retention physics (Boss, fork 7)

atmosphere-m.m1: the Sun is the reference star of the ozone-column fit, a stellar spectrum and not a body's composition
atmosphere-m.m4: the Venus phosphine claim is a test value for a design flag (GEN.525), never tuned

atmosphere-o.o1: solar twins are stars measured for thorium over hydrogen, a stellar sample
atmosphere-o.o2: the solar-twin scale of o1, a stellar sample

atmosphere-p.p1: the Sun's FUV and NUV flux is the reference of a stellar-flux fit
atmosphere-p.p3: the Sun's O3 lifetime is the comparison for the stellar-flux fit

comet-carbon-chain.carbon-chain-depleted-halley_type: the fractions are class statistics of observed comets (Cochran 2012, 2015), not one body; Halley and Jupiter are class names here
comet-carbon-chain.carbon-chain-depleted-jupiter_family: the fractions are class statistics of observed comets (Cochran 2012, 2015), not one body; Halley and Jupiter are class names here

comet-carbon-chain.carbon-chain-normal-long_period: the fractions are class statistics of observed comets (Cochran 2012, 2015), not one body; Halley and Jupiter are class names here

satellite-share.inner rubble pile with a satellite: near-Earth is the name of the asteroid population the binary fraction is measured in (Pravec 2006), a survey class, and the gate's cut is the survey's own

atmosphere-m.m2: O3 about 10 percent of the Earth's column (GEN.524 replaces it)

moon-satellites.no satellites: the rest of the row above it (1 minus the chance of a moon)

planet-satellites.no satellites: the rest of the captured-moon row above it (1 minus the chance of a moon)

satellite-share.belt rubble pile with a satellite: the binary fraction measured in near-Earth and main-belt asteroids, modelled by Jacobson 2016 (a measured small-body binary fraction replaces it)
